blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: After a long season of peace, the people of Israel turned away from the LORD again. They fell under the rule of Jabin, a king of Canaan. His captain was Sisera, and Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron. For twenty years he oppressed Israel hard, and the people cried out to the LORD.

verses.text: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time.

verses.text: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, Deborah was a prophetess and a judge. People came to her for wisdom and for justice. She sat under her palm tree up in the hill country, and Israel brought their troubles to her.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One day she sent for a man named Barak. She told him God had given him a command: gather ten thousand men at Mount Tabor. God would draw Sisera and his chariots down to the river Kishon and hand him over to Barak.

verses.text: And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.

segments.speaker: barak
segments.text: If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Barak would only go if Deborah went with him. Some folks hear fear in that. Others hear wisdom, a man who wanted God's prophet close by in the fight.

verses.text: And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

segments.speaker: deborah
segments.text: I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Deborah said yes. She also told him the honor would not be his, because the LORD would hand Sisera over to a woman. Then Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Barak gathered his ten thousand, and Deborah went up with him. When Sisera heard, he gathered every chariot and all his army by the river.

verses.text: And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which the LORD hath delivered Sisera into thine hand: is not the LORD gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

segments.speaker: deborah
segments.text: Up; for this is the day in which the LORD hath delivered Sisera into thine hand: is not the LORD gone out before thee?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Up. This is the day. Deborah did not hesitate. She saw what God was doing and told Barak to move. And Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.

verses.text: And the LORD discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera lighted down off his chariot, and fled away on his feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the LORD discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera lighted down off his chariot, and fled away on his feet.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When I say won't he do it, you say, yes he will. Won't he do it? [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Yes he will"] I said, won't he do it? [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Yes he will"] Twenty years of iron chariots, and the LORD went out before them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The LORD threw Sisera's great army into confusion. Those chariots that had scared Israel for twenty years were no help now. Sisera himself jumped down from his chariot and ran away on foot, and Barak's men chased the army down.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When it was over, Deborah and Barak sang together. Their song is one of the oldest in the whole Bible.

verses.text: Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, even I, will sing unto the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD God of Israel.

segments.speaker: deborah
segments.text: Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, even I, will sing unto the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD God of Israel.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Deborah was a judge, a prophet and a leader, called by God in a hard time. She sat under that palm tree and listened to folks' troubles, and when the day came, she stood up and said go. And her song gave the glory to the LORD.

pastor.note: Faithful to Judges 4:1-16 and 5:1-3; Jael's act not retold; Barak's request given two readings.

cultural.note: A woman judge with full authority; 'won't he do it' tied to the LORD going out before them, in the story's past.
